# Emails and direct messages

Identify the relationship and purpose: outreach, request, decision, update, announcement or sensitive discussion. Account for what the recipient already knows. Draft a subject when useful or requested; do not invent recipient details or claim previous contact.

Put the reason for writing or the reader's needed action early. Problem-led outreach should name a supported observation before offering help when that fits the brief. A routine announcement can start with the decision. A sensitive message may need acknowledgement or context before an ask. Do not reuse one opening formula across these purposes.

Include enough context to make the ask answerable: owner, requested decision, deadline and next step when supplied. Preserve exact dates, qualifications and unresolved points. Do not invent urgency, results, mutual connections or commitments.

Judge length by the recipient's task and explicit limits. A technical handoff may need detail; a cold email usually needs a narrow reason to respond. Remove duplicate setup and ceremonial sign-offs, while preserving warmth appropriate to the relationship. Producing a draft does not authorize sending it.
